title: Multinational HARMONi phase 3 trial record indexed in Lancet Oncology
publisher: Lancet Oncology record indexed by PubMed
specific_claims: The abstract describes a multinational randomized double-blind phase 3 comparison in 438 participants with advanced non-squamous EGFR-mutated NSCLC after third-generation EGFR-TKI progression.
The abstract reports median progression-free survival of 6.8 months versus 4.4 months, hazard ratio 0.52 (95% CI 0.41-0.66; p<0.0001).
The abstract reports median overall survival of 16.8 months versus 14.0 months, hazard ratio 0.79 (95% CI 0.62-1.01).
The PubMed parent record links an October 2026 correction whose substantive content was not reviewed.
supports: Existence and bounded abstract-level results of a distinct multinational HARMONi phase 3 trial.
A historical clinical evidence record for human review alongside, not in place of, the frozen HARMONi-A baseline.
does_not_support: An individual prognosis, hospital-specific outcome or treatment recommendation.
A cross-modality ranking or inference outside the enrolled population.
Automatic change to the frozen public research state or patient-specific stop point.
conflicts_counter_evidence: The public abstract was reviewed without full-text reanalysis.
The abstract records Summit Therapeutics funding.
A linked correction exists but its substantive effect was not established in this bounded review.
verification_scope: PubMed bibliographic record and abstract read; linked correction identified from the parent record but not substantively reviewed.
search_boundary: Bounded Sunday PubMed review of PMID 42636833, linked correction metadata and existing baseline PMID 42307937; no full-text or patient-level data review.
x_candidate_text: New historical evidence: a multinational phase 3 HARMONi trial reports longer PFS after third-generation EGFR-TKI progression. It does not establish personal prognosis or treatment choice. https://structurevidence.org/cases/nsq-nsclc-china/events/harmoni-multinational-phase3-2026/
next_minimum_verification: Review the correction text and full article before any substantive medical interpretation; preserve the patient-specific stop and frozen public evidence boundary.
